result.topic_en: Euler replaces x by x/y in the alternating series x/α − x²/β + x³/γ − … to get a two-variable continued fraction (Theorem IV), and applies it to l(1+x/y) and to √(x/y)·arctan√(x/y).
result.transcription:
158
§. 33. Quod si hic vbique loco $x$ scribamus $\frac{x}{y}$, vt habeamus hanc seriem:
$s = \frac{x}{\alpha y} - \frac{xx}{\beta yy} + \frac{x^3}{\gamma y^3} - \frac{x^4}{\delta y^4} + \text{etc.}$
tum fractio continua hinc nata erit
$\frac{x}{sy} = \alpha + \cfrac{\alpha\alpha x : y}{\beta - \frac{\alpha x}{y} + \cfrac{\beta\beta x : y}{\gamma - \frac{\beta x}{y} + \text{etc.}}}$
quae a fractionibus partialibus liberata dat
$\frac{x}{sy} = \alpha + \cfrac{\alpha\alpha x}{\beta y - \alpha x + \cfrac{\beta\beta xy}{\gamma y - \beta x + \cfrac{\gamma\gamma xy}{\delta y - \gamma x + \text{etc.}}}}$
vnde nascitur sequens
Theorema IV.
§. 34. Si proposita fuerit huiusmodi series infinita:
$s = \frac{x}{\alpha y} - \frac{xx}{\beta yy} + \frac{x^3}{\gamma y^3} - \frac{x^4}{\delta y^4} + \text{etc.}$
ex ea formari poterit ista fractio continua:
$\frac{x}{s} = \alpha y + \cfrac{\alpha\alpha xy}{\beta y - \alpha x + \cfrac{\beta\beta xy}{\gamma y - \beta x + \cfrac{\gamma\gamma xy}{\delta y - \gamma x + \cfrac{\delta\delta xy}{\epsilon y - \delta x + \text{etc}}}}}$
§. 35. Cum sit
$l(1 + \frac{x}{y}) = \frac{x}{y} - \frac{xx}{2yy} + \frac{x^3}{3y^3} - \frac{x^4}{4y^4} + \text{etc.}$
posito

159
posito $s = l(1 + \frac{x}{y})$ erit
$\alpha = 1,\ \beta = 2,\ \gamma = 3,\ \delta = 4$, etc.
hincque nascetur ista fractio continua:
$\frac{x}{l(1+\frac{x}{y})} = y + \cfrac{1xy}{2y - x + \cfrac{4xy}{3y - 2x + \cfrac{9xy}{4y - 3x + \text{etc.}}}}$
§. 36. Cum arcus cuius tangens $t$ hac serie exprimatur:
$\text{A. tang. } t = t - \frac{t^3}{3} + \frac{t^5}{5} - \frac{t^7}{7} + \frac{t^9}{9} - \text{etc.}$ erit
$t\,\text{A tang. } t = tt - \frac{t^4}{3} + \frac{t^6}{5} - \frac{t^8}{7} + \frac{t^{10}}{9} - \text{etc.}$
Nunc ponatur $tt = \frac{x}{y}$, ita vt sit $t = \sqrt{\frac{x}{y}}$, fietque
$\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}}.\ \text{A tang. } \sqrt{\frac{x}{y}} = \frac{x}{y} - \frac{xx}{3yy} + \frac{x^3}{5y^3} - \frac{x^4}{7y^4} + \text{etc.}$
Hinc ergo est $s = \sqrt{\frac{x}{y}}.\ \text{A tang. } \sqrt{\frac{x}{y}}$, tum vero
$\alpha = 1,\ \beta = 3,\ \gamma = 5,\ \delta = 7$, etc.,
quare fractio continua hinc nata erit
$\frac{\sqrt{xy}}{\text{A tang. } \sqrt{\frac{x}{y}}} = y + \cfrac{xy}{3y - x + \cfrac{9xy}{5y - 3x + \cfrac{25xy}{7y - 5x + \text{etc.}}}}$
Velut si fuerit $x = 1$ et $y = 3$, ob $\text{A tang. } \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{\pi}{6}$, habebitur ista fractio continua:
$6\sqrt{3}$

items.english: Theorem IV: If an infinite series of this kind is proposed, s = x/(αy) − x²/(βy²) + x³/(γy³) − x⁴/(δy⁴) + etc., then the following continued fraction can be formed from it: x/s = αy + ααxy/(βy − αx + ββxy/(γy − βx + …)).
